title: Prompt Engineering Tactics: Dan Cleary
talk_summary: Dan Cleary presents three prompt tactics: multi-persona prompting, source grounding via 'according to', and emotion prompts. The talk is a short vendor-adjacent overview with cited research numbers but little implementation detail or independent evaluation.

takeaways.what_they_do: In one prompt, assign several task-specific roles (e.g., author, critic, target user) to collaborate and show the exchange before the final answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it calls on various agents to work on a specific task when you prompt it. And those agents are designed for that specific task.

takeaways.what_they_do: Ground prompts to a named source by appending 'according to <source>' and require claims/findings to cite that source.
takeaways.evidence_quote: adding according to specified source will increase the chance that the model goes to that specific source to retrieve the information.

takeaways.what_they_do: Append a short emotional-importance stimulus to the end of a normal prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: add one of these emotional stimuli to the end of your normal prompt
